parsed.why: No trans-specific offence; hate-crime prosecutions, gender-identity anti-discrimination law and court-ordered protections operate, but top-level official hostility and high recorded discrimination keep it mid-band.

State-directed targeting: police app entrapment aimed at trans women, coerced anal exams, morality-law prison sentences, and removal of foreign nationals suspected of being gay or trans without charge.
No criminalisation, but no recourse at all: hostile attitudes toward visibly LGBTI, a killed activist, no functioning judicial protection; dated thin evidence resolves toward structural risk.
No trans-specific offence and courts sometimes grant recognition, but documented harassment of visibly trans people in provincial cities, rural violence and recent official hate speech persist.

Nationally enacted birth-sex restroom ban is universal exposure with no remedy, plus repealed anti-discrimination protection and rising anti-trans hate crime; torture convictions and health reform only partly offset.
